newsitem.title: UK: BA to brief staff on search for cost cutting.
newsitem.headline: BA to brief staff on search for cost cutting.

text.p: British Airways Plc intends to make a progress report to staff on Wednesday on progress for its ambitious "Step Change" efficiency drive aimed at cutting a billion stg from its annual cost base before the year 2000.
"It will be a further update and will involve giving a long term vision of the company and some of the processes that will be involved," a company spokesman said.
But he denied that the presentation would unveil plans for major job cuts as some recent newspaper reports have suggested.

Chief executive Robert Ayling announced earlier this year he intended to cut the airline's annual overheads by one billion stg in the next three years to offset continuing falls in average fare levels and rising costs of expansion.

As part of that move he said management was now looking at areas where it might consider buying in services if they were cheaper than in-house operations, and was looking at "all the ancillary services that go to make up the day-to-day operations of an airline, of which there are huge numbers."

"We will be making sure that wherever possible services provided within the company are at competitive rates...if that can't be achieved then we will buy in the services rather than provide them from within the company," he said.
